issues.t: Engine cradle (subframe) rusting through
issues.sym: Clunks from under the front of the vehicle, an engine that seems to shift, or a shop pointing out heavy rust or holes in the front subframe during an oil change or inspection. Some vans fail state safety inspection because of it.
issues.why: The front subframe that carries the engine and front suspension was not given enough rust-proof coating at the factory. In salted-road areas it can rot through, and in bad cases the engine and suspension mounting points lose their strength.
issues.next: Have the subframe inspected on a lift, especially on 2004-2005 vans from snowy states. If there are holes or flaking metal at the mounts, stop using the van for long trips until the cradle is replaced.

issues.t: Integrated power module (TIPM) failure
issues.sym: Stalling, headlights or dash lights going out, wipers or radio cutting out (often in rain), ABS and stability lights flickering on, or a no-start with just a click.
issues.why: The totally integrated power module is the under-hood fuse and relay box that also has its own circuit board. When it fails, it can cut power to the fuel pump and many other circuits at random.
issues.next: If several unrelated electrical things act up at once, ask the shop to test the TIPM before replacing individual parts. A replacement module must be programmed to the van.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or at a stop, sometimes with the dash lights flickering first. It often restarts, and dealers frequently find no stored code.
issues.why: Owners and shops have traced it to several causes: a corroded engine ground wire (the G103 ground bolted to the engine), a sticking EGR valve, a failing TIPM, or a weak crank sensor.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Note when it happens and whether any lights flicker. Ask the shop to check the engine ground connections and the EGR valve first, since those are simple fixes.

issues.t: Automatic transmission limp mode, slipping or shudder
issues.sym: The van gets stuck in one gear (limp mode), won't shift into 4th, slips, or shudders and vibrates at 30-40 mph.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in these vans can suffer from solenoid pack faults, leaking solenoid gaskets and a worn torque converter. A burst cooler hose can also drain the fluid.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. Have the codes read; a solenoid pack or torque converter repair is much less work than a full transmission if caught early.

issues.t: AWD transfer case (power transfer unit) failure
issues.sym: Loud grinding or whining from the front of the van, smoke or a burning smell, and fluid leaks near the transmission on all-wheel-drive models.
issues.why: The power transfer unit that sends power to the rear wheels on AWD Pacificas can wear out or crack its housing. Some owners blame worn engine mounts that let the drivetrain move too much.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear grinding with smoke. Have the transfer unit fluid and housing checked; replacement parts can be back-ordered, so get a quote early.

issues.t: Front-end clunks from tie rods, sway bar links and control arm bushings
issues.sym: Clunking or rattling over bumps, loose or wandering steering, uneven tire wear, or a knock when you start moving.
issues.why: Tie rod ends, sway bar links and bushings, and front lower control arm bushings on this heavy crossover wear quickly. Early 2004s had especially weak control arm bushings, and some owners replaced tie rods more than once.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. Sway bar links are a simple fix; worn tie rods need prompt replacement and a wheel alignment because a broken one causes loss of steering.

issues.t: Engine mounts tearing or leaking
issues.sym: A heavy clunk when shifting into drive or reverse or when you step on the gas, more vibration at idle, and an engine that visibly rocks.
issues.why: The fluid-filled engine mounts on the Pacifica tear and leak, and owners report replacing them more than once.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked with the engine running and in gear. Replace broken mounts soon, because a loose engine strains hoses, wiring, ground straps and the transmission.

issues.t: EGR valve sticking, rough idle and check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light (often code P0401 or P0404), rough or stumbling idle, hesitation, or stalling when coming to a stop.
issues.why: The electrically driven exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve gets clogged with carbon and stops opening or closing correctly.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning or replacing the EGR valve is usually a simple fix that also cures some stalling complaints.

issues.t: Radiator cracks and coolant leaks
issues.sym: Coolant puddles under the front, a sweet smell, the temperature gauge rising, or the low coolant warning.
issues.why: The plastic radiator tanks crack with age and heat cycles. Radiators and coolant hoses are among the most-replaced parts reported by Pacifica owners.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the system pressure-tested. Don't keep driving if it overheats.

issues.t: Fuel supply tube can separate and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell or fuel dripping under the hood.
issues.why: Some 2004 Pacificas were built with a fuel supply tube that was not made correctly and can pull apart, leaking fuel near hot engine parts.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside and do not drive. Check the VIN for recall 03V471; the dealer fix is free.

issues.t: Engine computer software can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls without warning while driving.
issues.why: A self-test for the EGR system in the engine computer software on some 2004 vans could make the engine stall.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recall 04V113. The dealer reprograms the engine computer for free.

issues.t: Halogen headlights can cut out (recall)
issues.sym: One or both headlights flicker or go out while driving, at first now and then and later for good.
issues.why: On some 2005 vans with halogen headlamps, a fault in the headlamp circuit can make the low beams stop working.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 05V066 and have it done for free. Avoid night driving if the headlights flicker.

issues.t: Fuel pump module and engine software can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving with no warning, sometimes after the fuel level runs low.
issues.why: Under some conditions the fuel pump module and the engine computer software can combine to starve the engine and stall it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recall 06V432. The dealer updates the software and fuel pump parts for free.

issues.t: Harsh shifting, jerking or slipping from the 9-speed automatic
issues.sym: Hard bangs or jerks when shifting at low speed, slipping with the engine revving before a gear catches, clunks into reverse or drive, or a Service Transmission message.
issues.why: The nine-speed automatic used with the gas engine is known for rough shift quality. Many cases are improved with software updates and a shift relearn; some vans need a valve body or a new transmission. Most reports involve 2017-2018 vans.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for transmission software updates and do an adaptive relearn first. If it slips or flashes Service Transmission, have it checked right away, ideally while still under warranty.

issues.t: Oil filter housing and oil cooler leak
issues.sym: Oil spots under the van, burning oil smell, oil or coolant seeping at the top back of the engine valley, or coolant loss.
issues.why: The Pentastar V6 uses a plastic oil filter housing with a built-in oil cooler. It can crack or its gaskets can leak oil and sometimes coolant.
issues.next: Have the leak traced before it soaks the belts and starter. The housing is replaced as a unit, often with an updated part.

issues.t: Ticking engine from worn rocker arms
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the top of the engine, sometimes with a misfire or check engine light.
issues.why: Rocker arm roller bearings on the Pentastar V6 can wear and seize, which also wears the camshaft lobe if left alone.
issues.next: Have a shop listen to it and check for misfire codes. Fixing worn rockers early can prevent a camshaft replacement.

issues.t: Service Hybrid System warning or no-start (hybrid)
issues.sym: A Service Hybrid System or Service Electric Vehicle System message, the van refusing to go into Ready mode, or loss of electric-only driving.
issues.why: Faults in the plug-in hybrid system, from the 12-volt battery and isolator post to the high-voltage battery and power electronics, trigger this warning. Several recalls cover parts of this system.
issues.next: Check for open recalls first. Hybrid parts carry a longer federal emissions warranty, so have a Chrysler dealer diagnose it before paying for repairs.

issues.t: Hybrid battery can catch fire while parked (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some vans show a hybrid system warning before an event.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery in some 2017-2018 Pacifica Hybrids can short internally and start a fire even when the van is off and not charging.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall 22V077 (replaced by 24V536). Until it is fixed, follow Chrysler's advice: don't charge it and park outside, away from buildings.

issues.t: Hybrid battery pack fire risk on 2020-2022 (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a fire.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery pack in some 2020-2022 Pacifica plug-in hybrids can catch fire, even when parked with the ignition off.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for recall 26V362. Don't charge the van and park it outside, away from buildings, until the remedy is done.

issues.t: Hybrid inverter can fail and stop the van (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power with a hybrid system warning; the van coasts and won't move under its own power.
issues.why: Diodes inside the power inverter module can be damaged by a voltage spike and shut down the drive system.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 17V371 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Gas engine may not restart properly after electric driving (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power when the engine should start, a check engine light, or a hot smell from the exhaust.
issues.why: After running on battery power, the gas engine may not restart correctly. Unburned fuel can then reach the catalytic converter and overheat it, with a small fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V740 and have the software updated for free.

issues.t: 12-volt battery isolator post can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell near the driver seat area, electrical warnings, or no-start.
issues.why: On plug-in hybrids the 12-volt isolator post under the driver area can develop high resistance and overheat, which can start a fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 20V334 and have the free fix done.

issues.t: Transmission wiring connector can shut off the engine (hybrid recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off unexpectedly and the van may lose drive power, often with warning lights.
issues.why: A wiring connector inside the hybrid transmission can short circuit and shut the engine down.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V010 and have the dealer repair it for free.

issues.t: Engine software can lose crank sensor timing and stall (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving and may restart.
issues.why: The engine control software can lose sync with the crankshaft position sensor signal on the 3.6L gas engine, which shuts the engine off.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recall 18V049. The software update is free.

issues.t: Engine computer power chip can fail and stall the van (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden stall while driving or a no-start, sometimes with several warning lights.
issues.why: A voltage regulator chip in the powertrain control module can fail, shutting the engine off or preventing it from starting.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recall 18V524 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Loose battery ground can cut power steering and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly feels very heavy, the engine stalls at a stop, or the stop/start system acts up.
issues.why: On gas vans with engine stop/start, the battery ground connection can loosen, causing intermittent loss of power steering assist or a stall.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recall 19V348. The dealer fixes the ground for free.

issues.t: Cruise control may not turn off (recall)
issues.sym: Cruise control stays on and holds or increases speed even after you press the brake or switch it off.
issues.why: A short circuit in the wiring can keep cruise control from canceling.
issues.next: If it happens, shift to neutral and brake firmly. Check the VIN for recall 18V332; the software update is free.

issues.t: Badly welded transmission part can cause loss of drive (recall)
issues.sym: The van suddenly loses power to the wheels while driving.
issues.why: A part inside the nine-speed transmission on some 2018 gas vans may have a poor weld that can break.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V492 and have it inspected and repaired for free.

issues.t: Right front lower control arm can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the right front, the van pulling, or sudden loss of steering control.
issues.why: On some 2018 Pacificas the right front lower control arm may come apart from the steering knuckle.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V143 and have it repaired for free. Don't drive if the front end clunks badly or the wheel looks out of line.

issues.t: Front axle shaft can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking, then loss of drive, or the van rolling even when in Park.
issues.why: Front half-shafts on some 2018 Pacificas were assembled wrong and can pull out of the CV joint.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park. Check the VIN for recall 18V493.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag connector may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly an airbag warning light, but often no sign at all.
issues.why: A side curtain airbag connector may not be fully seated, so the curtain airbag might not deploy in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V793; the dealer secures the connector for free.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may not hold pressure (recall)
issues.sym: No warning to the driver.
issues.why: Seams in the side curtain airbags may not be sealed well enough, so the airbags may deflate too soon in a crash or rollover.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V189 (which replaces 25V302 and 25V573) and get the free fix when parts are available.

issues.t: Second-row seat latch can stick open (recall)
issues.sym: The second-row seat rattles or doesn't feel locked to the floor.
issues.why: The latch that holds the second-row seat to the floor can stick open, so the seat may not be secured in a crash.
issues.next: Push and pull on the seat after moving it to be sure it's locked. Check the VIN for recall 22V181.

issues.t: Steering column module weld can stop the driver airbag (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly an airbag warning light.
issues.why: A poorly welded part in the steering column control module can break the circuit to the driver airbag.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V199 and have it replaced for free.

issues.t: Brake pedal sensor can disable stability control (recall)
issues.sym: Stability control or brake warning lights come on.
issues.why: A capacitor in the brake pedal position sensor can crack, causing loss of electronic stability control.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for recall 26V561 and have the sensor replaced for free.
